The most tradable sport nobody trades': Inside race prediction platform RPM

DM
By David Miller Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist • via The Race Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: The Race Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • RPM is the world’s first motorsport prediction platform, where every outcome of a race event becomes a tradable market.
  • Fans are able to buy and sell outcomes on every moment of a race at a moment’s notice.
  • Founder Ben Jarrett joined The Race Business as part of our Spotlight series of interviews to explain how he spotted a niche in the motorsport market - and how RPM itself could play a part in changing how fans consume motorsport.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DAVID MILLER Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist

Aerodynamic Efficiency & Motorsport Racecraft

In premier motorsport disciplines, millisecond gains represent months of high-intensity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) research. The developments reported by The Race underline how tire degradation curves, ground-effect aero seals, and power-unit energy recovery systems dictate race outcomes. Technical compliance under strict cost caps continues to test team engineering depth.

Big Picture: Upcoming grand prix telemetry and trackside upgrades will reveal which teams hold the definitive technical advantage.

RPM is the world’s first motorsport prediction platform, where every outcome of a race event becomes a tradable market. Fans are able to buy and sell outcomes on every moment of a race at a moment’s notice.

📌 The Core Development

Founder Ben Jarrett joined The Race Business as part of our Spotlight series of interviews to explain how he spotted a niche in the motorsport market - and how RPM itself could play a part in changing how fans consume motorsport.

“RPM is at the intersection of motorsport, content creation, and prediction markets,” says Jarrett.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Fans can essentially make predictions about every single facet of motorsport. And it’s an idea that was born out of a racetrack.

“I was racing GT4 cars, and I’m standing on the pitwall. Someone comes up and says: ‘10 bucks, he puts it into the wall at Turn 1’.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

“Everyone was standing there. I was in my suit, I had my hands on my helmet, and we were supposed to go out there for practice before qualifying and put a lap in.”

It was at that moment that Jarrett had the idea to open up motorsport prediction markets to fans and content creators.
